Fact-check reports

Chapter 15: historical context

247 table rows · source file V6b_ch15_history.md

V6b: Morrow (2013), Chapter 15 "The Covenants in Context" (printed pp. 333–352): fact-check of timeline rows and themes E–K

Book: John Andrew Morrow, The Covenants of the Prophet Muhammad with the Christians of the World (Angelico/Sophia Perennis, 2013). Scope: Chapter 15 only, covering:

  • the extraction's §2 timeline rows T76–T208;
  • its §4 claims C73–C174 (themes E–K);
  • the Chapter 15 items in its §7.

Biographical lifespans are left to the lifespan-table agent and listed at the end of §1.

Inputs:

  • Extraction: scratchpad/extract/08_ch13_ch17.md.
  • Book text: scratchpad/book/chunks/08_ch13_ch17.txt (book pages 333–352 = PDF pages 358–377). Every book quotation below was checked against this text.

How the work was done:

  • The lead agent covered early Islam, the Pact and Treaty of 'Umar, the early caliphs, the Ottomans and Mamluks, and the close of the chapter.
  • Helper A covered al-Andalus, Granada and the Moriscos.
  • Helper C covered the conduct of other powers, law and civilisation, and the Qur'an and hadith citations.
  • Working files are in scratchpad/v6b_work/: part_M_early_ottoman.md, part_A_andalus.md and part_C_powers_law.md. Downloads are in dlA/, dlB/, dlC/ and dlM/.
  • Rows taken from helper files keep their original id in brackets, e.g. [A16] or [C7a].

Evidence rules:

  • Every verdict rests on a page or full text that was actually opened (WebFetch, or a curl download of the full text). Search-engine snippets were never used as evidence.
  • "OL search-inside" (Helper C) means verbatim OCR excerpts returned by the Open Library full-text API for a lending-only book. These are verbatim but partial.
  • Wikipedia is marked "(lead)" wherever it appears, and is used only as a lead or for uncontroversial dates.
  • Earlier verification files were reused and cited by name, for example V5 for the Jerusalem surrender dates, V1b for the campaign counts, and Part B for the coinage.

Verdict labels: Consistent / Minor difference / Inconsistent / Disputed among sources / Unverified / Opinion. Before any item was marked Inconsistent, OCR error and AH-to-CE conversion were ruled out and a second source was sought.

Row keys: T = extraction §2 timeline row; C = extraction §4 claim; S7-n = extraction §7 item.

1. Verification table

1.1 Theme E: early Islam and treatment of non-Muslims (pp. 333–336)
# Book claim (page) Verdict What independent sources say Source URLs
T77 Vernet (1992: 176): "Muslim tolerance undoubtedly contributed to the absorption of Arab culture … by the Christian faithful" (p. 333) Unverified quotation Vernet 1992 not opened. —
T78 Prophet launched "68 military campaigns", "no more than 1,000 casualties on all sides" (p. 333) Campaign count: Minor difference (compilers differ). Casualty total: Unverified, and in tension with the traditional figures Campaign counts (prior check V1b T122): Ibn Ishaq gives 27 raids + 38 expeditions = 65 (or 27 + 35); Ibn Sa'd gives 27 + 47 = 74 (Guillaume pp. 659–660; Ibn Sa'd II p. 2). No opened source gives "68". On casualties (V1b T124): the Qurayza execution alone is put at 600–700, "some put the figure as high as 800 or 900" (Ibn Ishaq, Guillaume p. 464); Kister collects 400–900. Add the Meccan dead at Badr (c. 50–70) and Uhud, and the total exceeds 1,000 unless the Qurayza tradition is rejected. V1b_ch1_second_half.md (T122, T124), citing https://archive.org/details/GuillaumeATheLifeOfMuhammad and Kister, JSAI 8 (1986) via http://web.archive.org/web/20250118072808/http://www.kister.huji.ac.il/sites/default/files/banu_qurayza.pdf
T81 'Umar forbade plunder; conquered lands left to cultivators, who paid rent to the state (Armstrong 31) (p. 334) Consistent in substance; Armstrong's page not opened Abu Yusuf's Kitab al-Kharaj records 'Umar's decision not to divide the Sawad among the conquerors; Britannica credits 'Umar with the diwan and the garrison cities. Armstrong 2000 p. 31 not opened. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenITI/0200AH/master/data/0182AbuYusufYacqub/0182AbuYusufYacqub.Kharaj/0182AbuYusufYacqub.Kharaj.Shamela0026333-ara1 ; https://web.archive.org/web/2026/https://www.britannica.com/biography/Umar-I
T82 Garrison towns ("ansar", as printed) were built at Kufah, Basrah, Qum and Fustat (Armstrong 31) (p. 334) Inconsistent for Qum; "ansar" is a misprint for amsar Britannica, "'Umar I": "He also established the garrison cities of Al-Fusṭāṭ in Egypt and Basra and Kūfah in Iraq" (Qum is not listed). Encyclopaedia Iranica, "Qom": a first tentative conquest in 23/644 by Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, after which "the area remained largely untouched for 60 years"; "the first permanent settlement of Arab settlers in Qom took place during the revolts of … 66-77/685-96". So Qum was not an 'Umar-era garrison town. The error may come from Armstrong's text, which was not opened. https://web.archive.org/web/2026/https://www.britannica.com/biography/Umar-I ; https://iranicaonline.org/articles/qom
T83 Muslims "were very much a minority for centuries" in their empire (p. 334) Unverified (plausible; not checked) No opened source. Conversion-rate studies (e.g. Bulliet 1979) were not opened. —

T85 Glubb (376): from 700 onwards the "'Arab' armies" were regular troops drawn from the indigenous peoples (p. 334) Unverified quotation Glubb not opened. —
T87 / C80 Donner (115; 248): no archaeological evidence of widespread destruction; churches built after the conquest (p. 334) Unverified quotation Donner 1981 is lending-only; the 2010 book was not opened. https://archive.org/details/earlyislamicconq0000donn (restricted)
C81 "Lebanon is still almost half Christian" (Brockopp 10) (p. 334) Inconsistent with current estimates (dated claim) US State Dept, 2023 Report on International Religious Freedom: Lebanon: Statistics Lebanon "estimates that 69.3 percent of the citizen population is Muslim … and that 30.5 percent of the population is Christian". There has been no census since 1932. Estimates from around 2010 (higher figures) were not opened. https://www.ecoi.net/de/dokument/2111903.html
T88 / C82–C84 Berkey 97; Ratliff 34; O'Shea 15 (pp. 334–335) Unverified quotations Not opened. —
T89 / C82 Yeshuyab III: "They have not attacked the Christian religion, but rather they have commended our faith, honoured our priests … and conferred benefits on churches and monasteries" (qtd. Armour) (p. 335) Consistent quotation; context omitted Isho'yahb III, Ep. 14C (Duval, CSCO 12, Latin version p. 182): "nec solum christianum religionem non impugnant, verum etiam fidem nostram commendant, sacerdotes sanctosque Domini nostri honorant, et in ecclesias coenobiaque beneficia conferunt." The same passage rebukes the Christians of Mazun (Oman) for abandoning their faith. The Arabs "did not compel them" but required them to give up half their property; they apostatised to keep the other half. GEDSH: Isho'yahb III was catholicos 649–659. https://archive.org/details/DuvalIshoyahb (file "CSCO 12_djvu.txt") ; https://gedsh.bethmardutho.org/Ishoyahb-III-of-Adiabene
T90 Bishop of Adiabene, "writing just after the Muslim invasion (650-660 CE)": new masters "not nearly as bad as expected" … (Fortuescue [Fortescue] 92) (p. 335) Consistent with Fortescue (OCR "Fortuescue"). Possible duplication of witnesses (inference) Fortescue, Lesser Eastern Churches (1913) p. 92: "So a Bishop of Adiabene, writing just after the Moslem invasion (650-660), says that the new masters are by no means so bad as they are thought to be, that they are not far removed from Christianity, honour its clergy and protect its Churches" (n. 7: Assemani, BO III.i p. 131). The same paragraph introduces such reports as "Various legends grew up later, or were made deliberately to persuade the Moslem conqueror …". It names the 1630 "Testament of Mohammed" (Sionita) among them. GEDSH says Isho'yahb III was metropolitan of Arbela (Adiabene) and catholicos 649–659. The "Bishop of Adiabene (650–660)" may therefore be Isho'yahb III himself, making it the same witness as T89. This is my inference; Assemani was not opened. https://archive.org/details/lessereasternchu00fortuoft ; https://gedsh.bethmardutho.org/Ishoyahb-III-of-Adiabene
T91 John bar Penkaye "(7th century CE)": "there was no distinction between pagan and Christian … the believer was not known from a Jew" (qtd. Hoyland 2000: 293) (p. 335) Date Consistent; quotation Unverified GEDSH: "Yoḥannan bar Penkaye (late 7th cent.)", author of the Book of the main events. The quotation and its context were not checked: Brock's translation and Hoyland were not opened, and Mingana's Sources syriaques scan is Syriac only. https://gedsh.bethmardutho.org/Yohannan-bar-Penkaye ; https://archive.org/details/sourcessyriaques12ming
T92 Mamdani 25: "the point of the Crusades was not to convert Muslims but to exterminate them" (p. 335) Attribution Unverified. As history, Contested (see §4) Britannica, "Crusades": "military expeditions … organized by western European Christians in response to centuries of Muslim wars of expansion. Their objectives were to check the spread of Islam, to retake control of the Holy Land …, to conquer pagan areas, and to recapture formerly Christian territories". https://web.archive.org/web/2026/https://www.britannica.com/event/Crusades
T93 / C86 Abu Bakr renewed the Prophet's covenant with Najran; text "found in the Kitab al-kharaj by Abu Yusuf" (qtd. Danios) (p. 335) Consistent Abu Yusuf, al-Kharaj (ed. Sa'd & Sa'd, p. 85), "Kitab Abi Bakr li-ahl Najran": "ajarahum bi-jiwar Allah wa-dhimmat Muhammad … 'ala anfusihim wa-aradihim wa-millatihim wa-amwalihim wa-hashiyatihim wa-'ibadatihim wa-gha'ibihim wa-shahidihim wa-asaqifatihim wa-ruhbanihim wa-biya'ihim wa-kull ma taht aydihim min qalil aw kathir". The text continues "no bishop shall be moved from his bishopric nor monk from his monastic state … in fulfilment of all that Muhammad wrote for them". The book's English matches closely. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenITI/0200AH/master/data/0182AbuYusufYacqub/0182AbuYusufYacqub.Kharaj/0182AbuYusufYacqub.Kharaj.Shamela0026333-ara1
T95 / C87 'Umar's Jerusalem guarantee (qtd. Haya 5): lives, belongings, churches, crucifixes; churches not inhabited or destroyed; no forced conversion (p. 335) Consistent (a paraphrase of the Tabari text) Tabari XII (tr. Friedmann) pp. 191–192: "safety for themselves, for their property, their churches, their crosses … Their churches will not be inhabited [by Muslims] and will not be destroyed … They will not be forcibly converted. No Jew will live with them in Jerusalem." The book's short version omits the Jewish clause and the poll tax. https://archive.org/details/the-history-of-al-tabari (Tabari_Volume_12_djvu.txt)
T96 / S7-5 Patriarch "Solonio" showed 'Umar the holy sites "in 659 CE"; 'Umar declined to pray in the Holy Sepulchre (p. 335) Inconsistent (date). The prayer story is later tradition. "Solonio" is a name error 'Umar died on 3 Nov 644 (Britannica). The surrender of Jerusalem is dated variously 634/5–638 (V5 §2: Theophanes AM 6127; Tabari "year 15" = 636/7; Kaegi 637; Baladhuri and El-Awaisi Muharram 17/Feb 638). The patriarch was Sophronius (d. 11 Mar 639). Neither calendar conversion nor OCR explains "659", which is the book's own date for Mu'awiya (T98) and was probably copied from it. Gibbon (ch. 51) tells the refusal-to-pray story: "the caliph refused to perform his devotions, and contented himself with praying on the steps of the church of Constantine … 'the Moslems of a future age would have infringed the treaty under color of imitating my example'". Gibbon draws on later Arabic chronicles of Jerusalem (via Ockley, n. 84). This check found no seventh-century source for the story; it was not traced to its earliest attestation. https://web.archive.org/web/2026/https://www.britannica.com/biography/Umar-I ; V5_assyrian_armenian.md (§2, T69, C167) ; https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/735/pg735.txt
T96 (custody) 'Umar entrusted the Holy Sepulchre to 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, "whose descendants, known by the family name of Nuseibeh, continue to administer the holy site to this day" (p. 335) Disputed among sources (family tradition; the details conflict) Nuseibeh family website: "One of the great ancestors … was 'Ubada Ibn Al-Samet … appointed as a governor by 'Umr … Another was Abdullah, the son of Nusaybah … It is said that the keys … were placed in the custody of the family during this period. It is also said that the keys were placed in its custody during the times of … Saladin". The same site also says "At least since the time of Saladin … (1187-1517)". In Haj Taher Nusseibeh's narrative, 'Umar entrusted the keys to "Abdullah Ben Nusseibeh", not to 'Ubada. Jerusalem Story (2024, from the family history): 'Umar assigned "Abdullah ibn Nusseibeh", and the family was absent from 1099 to 1187. Since 1878 a status quo has applied: the Joudeh family holds the key and the Nusseibehs open the door. The family "administers" only the door, not the site, which is run by the Christian communities. No independent early source was found. https://nuseibehfamily.net/introduction ; https://nuseibehfamily.net/articles/12-articles/68-the-holy-sepulcher-in-jerusalem ; https://www.jerusalemstory.com/en/article/nusseibeh-family-khazraj-roots-grew-and-blossomed-jerusalem
T97 'Uthman "was even married to a Jacobite Christian" (Betts 9) (p. 335) Minor difference (misleading) Tabari XV (tr. Humphreys): "In this year, 'Uthman married Na'ilah bint al-Farafisah. She was a Christian, but converted to Islam before he consummated the marriage." The Islamweb history text has the same: "She had been a Christian and embraced Islam before he consummated the marriage." "Jacobite" is not in these sources. https://archive.org/details/the-history-of-al-tabari (Tabari_Volume_15_djvu.txt) ; https://hadithunlocked.com/history:1991
T98 Mu'awiyah prayed at Golgotha, Gethsemane and the grave of the Virgin "after becoming 'king' in Jerusalem in 659" (Crone and Cook 11) (p. 335) Minor difference (Seleucid year spans 659/660) Maronite Chronicle (Chronica Minora II, CSCO, Latin): "Anno 971°, Constantis 18°, congregati sunt Arabes multi Hierosolymis, et regem creaverunt Mo'awiam: is adscendit in montem Golgotha, ibi sedit et oravit, et ivit ad hortum Gethsemani, et descendit ad sepulcrum beatae Mariae". The allegiance followed "eodem anno, mense tamuz" (July). AG 971 = Oct 659 – Sep 660, so the Tammuz allegiance falls in July 660. Hagarism p. 11 was not opened. https://archive.org/details/csco-1-6
T99 / C(p.336) "The Caliph 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Marwan (d. 705 CE) was also known for his love of the Christians" (Crone & Cook 11) (p. 336) Inconsistent (title). Characterisation Disputed He was governor of Egypt, never caliph. LC authority heading: "ʻAbd al-ʻAzīz ibn Marwān, Governor of Egypt, -704 or 705". Fortescue p. 229 (a source the book cites elsewhere): "'Abdu-l'Aziz suddenly demanded a hundred thousand pieces of gold from [Patriarch John III], and burned his feet with hot coals"; he "had a census of all monks made, imposed a special tax on them, and forbade anyone in future to become a monk". https://www.islam-anatolia.ac.uk/data/documents/auth/lccn:n90689938 ; https://archive.org/details/lessereasternchu00fortuoft
C79, C85, C88 Indigenous Muslim troops were not "lackeys"; defence of the homeland is "part of din" (reported hadith); conquests were for "liberation, taxation, and invitation to Islam"; Mu'awiyah "a person of little tolerance towards many Muslims" (pp. 334–335) Opinion (the hadith was not traced) — —
1.2 Qur'an and hadith citations in the chapter (helper C)
# Book claim (page) Verdict What independent sources say Source URLs
C73 / S7-15 [C12a] "According to a saying of the Prophet recounted in the Sahih Bukhari, 'Whoever oppresses a Jew or a Christian I will testify against him on the Day of Judgment.'" (p. 333) Inconsistent (wrong collection and wording) A full-text search of the English Sahih al-Bukhari (hadith-api edition) found no such hadith. The nearest Bukhari text is no. 3166: "Whoever killed a person having a treaty with the Muslims [mu'ahad] shall not smell the smell of Paradise". The nearest in wording is Abu Dawud 3052: "Beware, if anyone wrongs a contracting man [mu'ahid], or diminishes his right, or forces him to work beyond his capacity, or takes from him anything without his consent, I shall plead for him [Arabic: fa-ana ḥajījuhu] on the Day of Judgment". Grades: Albani "Sahih"; Muhyi al-Din Abd al-Hamid "Sahih"; Zubair Ali Zai "Da'if". It concerns any person under covenant, not specifically Jews or Christians. A third version, "Whoever harms a dhimmi, I am his adversary…" (Suyuti, Jam' al-Jawami' 20073a, from al-Khatib < Ibn Mas'ud), is weak or baseless according to the Dorar summary of critics. Ahmad b. Hanbal (via Ibn al-Jawzi): "laysa lahu asl"; al-Khatib: "munkar al-isnad"; Ibn Hajar: the chain contains Ibn al-Tallaj, accused of fabrication; Albani, Da'if al-Jami' 5314: "Da'if"; Ahmad Shakir: no basis in this wording, "but its meaning is reported with acceptable chains"; al-Zarqani (outlier): "hasan". cdn.jsdelivr.net hadith-api (eng-bukhari, eng-abudawud); sunnah.com/bukhari:3166, /abudawud:3052; hadithunlocked.com/suyuti:20073a; dorar.net API
C74 [C12b] "I am the prophet of mercy, I am the prophet of battle" (p. 334) Consistent (abridged) Shama'il al-Tirmidhi 367 (Hudhayfa): "I am Muhammad; I am Ahmad; I am the Prophet of Mercy and the Prophet of Repentance; … and the Prophet of the Fierce Battles [nabiyy al-malāḥim]". Grades: "Hasan Isnad" (Zubair Ali Za'i); Albani, Mukhtasar al-Shama'il 316: hasan. Abu Musa's version, "nabiyy al-rahma, nabiyy al-malhama", is in Musnad Ahmad (Arna'ut: "isnaduhu sahih", no. 19525) and Ibn Hibban 6314 (Arna'ut: sahih by the criteria of Bukhari and Muslim). Ibn Taymiyya calls it "ma'ruf". Sahih Muslim 2355 (Abu Musa) has "the Prophet of repentance, and the Prophet of Mercy" but not "battle". The book's citation chain (Ibn Taymiyya, Dhahabi, Tabari, Mawardi via Hamidullah) is plausible, but I did not open those works. sunnah.com/shamail:367; dorar.net API; hadith-api eng-muslim
C115 / S7-16 [C11a] Qur'an quoted as "(5:72)": "those who believe, those who follow Jewish scriptures, the Christians, the Sabians, and any who believe in God and the Last Day, and do good, all shall have their reward with their Lord and they will not come to fear or grief." (p. 341) Inconsistent (wrong reference) 5:72 actually reads (Yusuf Ali): "They do blaspheme who say: 'Allah is Christ the son of Mary.' … Whoever joins other gods with Allah, - Allah will forbid him the garden, and the Fire will be his abode." The quoted wording is 2:62 (Yusuf Ali: "Those who believe (in the Qur'an), and those who follow the Jewish (scriptures), and the Christians and the Sabians, - any who believe in Allah and the Last Day, and work righteousness, shall have their reward with their Lord; on them shall be no fear, nor shall they grieve."). The close parallel 5:69 lacks "reward with their Lord" and puts Sabians before Christians. The book itself cites this wording correctly as 2:62 on p. 374. api.quran.com v4 by_key 2:62, 5:69, 5:72 (translations 22, 85, 20)
C77 and other Qur'an refs [C11b] 109:6 "To you your religion and to me mine" (p. 334); 2:256 and 29:46 (p. 339, inside a covenant text); 49:13 (p. 346); 22:40 (p. 346); 9:12 (p. 352 epigraph) Consistent (all six references match their wording) 109:6, Yusuf Ali: "To you be your Way, and to me mine". 2:256 and 29:46 match Yusuf Ali verbatim. 49:13 is a free rendering of the verse's content. 22:40 matches Yusuf Ali (second half of the verse). The 9:12 epigraph matches Saheeh International, except "fight" where the current API text has "combat"; Pickthall and Hilali-Khan also use "fight". api.quran.com v4 by_key for each verse (translations 22, 85, 20, 19, 203)
C135 [C12d] "O people, I am leaving among you that which if you hold on to you shall never go astray: the Book of Allah and my kindred, my household" (p. 345) Consistent with Tirmidhi 3786. Gradings differ. Tirmidhi 3786 (Jabir, Day of 'Arafa): "'O people! Indeed, I have left among you, that which if you hold fast to it, you shall not go astray: The Book of Allah and my family, the people of my house'" (Arabic: kitab Allah wa-'itrati ahl bayti). Tirmidhi himself: "hasan gharib min hadha al-wajh". Albani: Sahih; Bashar Awad Ma'ruf: Hasan; Zubair Ali Zai: Da'if; Darussalam (sunnah.com): Sahih. Tirmidhi 3788 (Zayd b. Arqam): adds "One of them is greater than the other … they shall not split until they meet at the Hawd"; Tirmidhi: "hasan gharib". Muslim 2408 (Zayd b. Arqam, Ghadir Khumm) has different wording: "I am leaving among you two weighty things: the one being the Book of Allah …" and then "I remind you (of your duties) to the members of my family". It contains no "you will not go astray" clause tied to the household. sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3786, /tirmidhi:3788; hadith-api eng-tirmidhi, eng-muslim
T208 [C12c] "Islam began as something strange, and it shall return to being something strange, so give glad tidings to the strangers" (Muslim) (p. 351) Consistent Sahih Muslim 145 (Abu Hurayra): "Islam initiated as something strange, and it would revert to its (old position) of being strange. so good tidings for the stranger"; Arabic "بدأ الإسلام غريبا وسيعود كما بدأ غريبا فطوبى للغرباء". Muslim 146 (Ibn 'Umar) is a variant. sunnah.com/muslim:145; hadith-api eng-muslim

Translation: the book has "Nothing shall be taken from them after their crops have been harvested"; Friedmann has "Nothing will be taken from them before their harvest is reaped", which reverses the meaning. The book also omits the clause on "villagers (ahl al-ard) who were in Jerusalem before the killing of so-and-so". AH 15 = Feb 636 – Jan 637, which no book page converts. https://archive.org/details/the-history-of-al-tabari (Tabari_Volume_12_djvu.txt)

Minor difference (name: Seleucia) PO 13 p. 620 [300]: "aux habitants de Séleucie et de Nahr Bir", with a note on Nahr Bir: "Lecture conjecturale". p. 623 [303]: "Témoins 'Othman ben Affan et El-Mogheira ben So'ba en la dix-septième année de l'Hégire"; note 2: "La dix-septième année de l'Hégire commençait en 638". T114 Khalid b. al-Walid promised Christians they could ring church bells "at any time, day or night", except at Muslim prayer times, and take out crosses on holy days (qtd. Haya 5) (pp. 339–340) Consistent, with context narrowed Abu Yusuf, al-Kharaj p. 160: Khalid's peace with the people of 'Anat: no church to be demolished; "an yadribu nawaqisahum fi ayy sa'a sha'u min layl aw nahar illa fi awqat al-salawat, wa-'ala an yukhriju al-sulban fi ayyam 'idihim". The same treaty adds: "he stipulated that they host the Muslims for three days and guide them". The same terms were then given to al-Naqib, al-Kawathil and Qarqisiya. It is a local surrender treaty (with hospitality and guide duties), not a general promise "to the Christians". https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenITI/0200AH/master/data/0182AbuYusufYacqub/0182AbuYusufYacqub.Kharaj/0182AbuYusufYacqub.Kharaj.Shamela0026333-ara1

T116 / S7-6 Battle of the Masts, 655 CE; Mu'awiyah organised the navy "while governor of Syria under the Caliph 'Umar"; crews included Monophysite, Coptic and Jacobite sailors (p. 340) Date: Disputed among sources (655 is mainstream). "Under 'Umar": Inconsistent. Crews: Unverified Britannica, "Mu'awiyah I": appointed governor of Damascus by 'Umar in 640; campaigns led to Cyprus (649), Rhodes (654) and "a devastating defeat of the Byzantine navy off the coast of Lycia in Anatolia (655)". Tabari XV: Abu Ma'shar dates it to AH 34 (654–55) and al-Waqidi to AH 31 (651–52). Baladhuri (Hitti I pp. 235–236): "Mu'awiyah had asked 'Umar's permission to lead a naval expedition, but 'Umar refused"; 'Uthman allowed it in AH 28. The navy and the battle therefore belong to 'Uthman's caliphate (644–656), after 'Umar died in 644. Theophanes (tr. Mango & Scott), under AM 6146 [AD 653/4] ("Outhman, 9th year"), says Mu'awiya had the armament built at Tripolis and named "Aboulauar" (Abu'l-A'war) commander; the editors date the battle of Phoinix to 655. Their notes add Michael the Syrian (AG 966, AH 35), the Chronicle of 1234 (AH 37) and Elias of Nisibis (AH 34). https://web.archive.org/web/20261027002919/https://www.britannica.com/biography/Muawiyah-I ; https://archive.org/details/the-history-of-al-tabari (vol. 15) ; https://archive.org/details/originsofislamic00balarich ; https://archive.org/details/chronicle-of-theophanes-the-confessor
